# `starhermit:weather`

Engine **1.40.0** (host API 1.40), the latest release. Generated from the release's `starhermit.d.ts`; `starhermit types` writes the same file into your game. [All modules](index.md).

```ts
import { … } from "starhermit:weather";
```

### WindTier

*type*

```ts
export type WindTier = "full" | "reduced" | "minimal" | "off";
```

### WindSettings

*interface*

```ts
export interface WindSettings { … }
```

- `speed?: number;`

  The mean wind 10 m up, m/s, 0 to 100 (default 5).

- `direction?: number;`

  The way it blows toward, radians from +x toward +z (default 0).

- `gustiness?: number;`

  Gusts and lulls, 0..1 (default 0.5).

- `turbulence?: number;`

  How far the direction wanders from place to place, 0..1 (default 0.3).

- `seed?: number;`

  Which wind: a whole number below 2^24 (default 1).

### SwayOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface SwayOptions { … }
```

- `kind?: "grass" | "tree";`

  "grass" (default): bends from y = 0 in its mesh along an arc (keeping its length) by an angle growing with the drag (the wind's speed squared) until it lies over, shimmering, its normals tilted with it. "tree": the trunk leans with the drag and sways from its base at the mesh's origin, branches (beyond 0.5 m of the axis) swing behind it by the way they point, every part of the tree reading the wind at its trunk.

- `flutter?: boolean | "custom";`

  Leaves flutter: true every vertex, "custom" by the geometry's `custom.z` weight with `custom.y` the branch's phase (starhermit-trees' vertex stream), false (default) none.

- `strength?: number;`

  How far the wind bends it (default 1).

- `flutterStrength?: number;`

  How strongly leaves flutter (default 1).

- `shadows?: "swayed" | "rest";`

  "swayed" (default): shadow maps see the swayed pose; "rest": the pose at rest.

### WIND\_HOOK\_WGSL

*const*

```ts
export const WIND_HOOK_WGSL: string;
```

WGSL for a material's hooks: `wind_sample(xz: vec2f) -> vec4f` (this frame's wind 10 m up in xy and last frame's in zw, m/s along x and z), `wind_at(xz)` and `wind_at_previous(xz)`; give the hooks a field's `uniforms`. Declare it once in a material's parts.

### WIND\_SWAY\_WGSL

*const*

```ts
export const WIND_SWAY_WGSL: string;
```

`wind_sway(v: Vertex) -> Vertex` for a vertex hook (after WIND\_HOOK\_WGSL); `sway` sets its uniform and defines.

### WIND\_FIELD\_WGSL

*const*

```ts
export const WIND_FIELD_WGSL: string;
```

`wind_velocity(a, b, c: vec4f, xz: vec2f) -> vec2f`, the GPU twin of `velocityAt`, from `snapshot`'s three vec4s.

### WindField

*class*

```ts
export class WindField { … }
```

- `constructor(settings?: WindSettings);`

- `speed: number;`

  The settings; changing one (or `set`) keeps the gusts already in the air where they are, carried on at the new mean from `time`.

- `direction: number;`
- `gustiness: number;`
- `turbulence: number;`
- `seed: number;`
- `set(settings: WindSettings, time?: number): this;`

- `readonly params: Float64Array;`

  The CPU twin's 8 numbers (starhermit-weather-kernel's `wind_params`).

- `readonly uniforms: WindUniforms;`

- `maxTier: WindTier;`

  The best tier the game allows (default "full").

- `readonly tier: WindTier;`

  The tier of the last `update`. When the device (no float targets) or the lowest graphics level lowers it below `maxTier`, Options → Graphics carries a note saying so.

- `static deviceTier(): WindTier;`

  The best tier this device and graphics level allow, whatever `maxTier` says. `renderer.capabilities` stays three.js's device facts (`floatRenderable`, which this follows from); the tier is this module's policy, so it is reported here rather than there.

- `readonly texture: Texture | null;`

  The field (RGBA: this frame's wind in rg, last frame's in ba; RGBA8 scaled by `uniforms.windEye.w`), or null without one.

- `time: number;`

  Seconds of the wind's clock; `update` advances it.

- `velocityAt(x: number, z: number, time?: number, target?: Vector2): Vector2;`

  The wind 10 m up at (x, z) at `time` (default `this.time`): m/s along x in `x` and along z in `y`. Deterministic on every runtime.

- `velocities(points: ArrayLike<number>, time?: number, out?: Float32Array): Float32Array;`

  The wind at (x, z) pairs, two numbers a point.

- `snapshot(time?: number, out?: Float32Array): Float32Array;`

  The 12 numbers `WIND_FIELD_WGSL` takes for the wind at `time`.

- `update(camera?: Object3D | null, delta?: number): void;`

  Advances the clock by `delta` (default the frame's), centres the field on `camera` and fills it. Once a frame, before rendering.

- `readonly shaderError: string | null;`

- `sway<T extends Material>(material: T, options?: SwayOptions): T;`

  Adds the sway vertex hook to `material`'s hooks (after a vertex hook it has); set its own hooks first.

- `swayMesh<T extends Mesh>(mesh: T, options?: SwayOptions): T;`

  `sway` for the mesh's materials, and its geometry's bounding sphere grown by how far the wind can carry it (once a geometry).

- `dispose(): void;`

## The weather and its visuals (host API 1.40, WEATHER\_EFFECTS\_MINOR)

Solstice's weather model and its effects: volumetric clouds as a SkyAtmosphere layer, rain kept from under roofs, wet surfaces and puddles, lightning and thunder. The CPU parts (the model, its easing and cycle, the cloud noise, rain's accumulators, strikes) are starhermit-weather's: the same numbers natively and in browsers. Distances are metres (a world unit is a metre).

### WeatherKind

*type*

```ts
export type WeatherKind = "clear" | "cirrus" | "fair" | "broken" | "overcast" | "storm";
```

### WeatherSettings

*interface*

```ts
export interface WeatherSettings { … }
```

- `coverage?: number;`

  Share of the sky the main layer covers, 0..1 (default 0.3).

- `cloudType?: number;`

  0 flat stratus, 0.5 stratocumulus, 1 heaped cumulus (0.9).

- `base?: number;`

  The cloud base above the ground, m (1200), and the layer's depth, m (1600).

- `thickness?: number;`

- `density?: number;`

  How thick the cloud is inside: 1 ordinary, more rain-bearing (1).

- `cirrus?: number;`

  Share of the sky high cirrus covers, 0..1 (0.15).

- `windSpeed?: number;`

  The wind at cloud height, m/s (7), and the compass bearing it blows from, degrees (250; 270 a westerly, toward +X; north is −Z).

- `windFrom?: number;`

- `gusts?: number;`

  How gusty the wind near the ground is and how much its direction wanders, 0..1 (0.4 each).

- `turbulence?: number;`

- `evolution?: number;`

  How fast clouds grow and fade (1).

- `rain?: number;`

  How heavily it rains, 0..1 (0; 1 a 40 mm/h downpour).

- `thunder?: number;`

  Lightning strikes a minute (0).

### Weather

*class*

What the sky is doing, in Solstice's `.weather` text: a setting a line (`coverage 0.3`, `type 0.9`, `base 1200`, `thickness 1600`, `density 1`, `cirrus 0.15`, `wind speed=7 from=250 gusts=0.45 turbulence=0.45`, `evolution 1`, `rain 0`, `thunder 0`), `#` starting a comment; every setting has a default. Fields are kept as binary32 (`toArray`).

*class*

### WeatherCycle

*class*

A sky that changes by itself: two to five minutes in a kind, then one that could follow it (clear to fair or cirrus, fair to broken or clear, broken to overcast or fair, overcast to storm or broken, storm to broken or overcast, cirrus to fair or broken), each change easing in over 90 s. Deterministic for its seed.

- `readonly current: WeatherKind;`
- `advance(seconds: number): WeatherKind | null;`

### CloudTier

*type*

```ts
export type CloudTier = "full" | "quarter" | "dome" | "off";
```

"full": half resolution with temporal reprojection (last frame's view-projection), skipping texels geometry covers (it reads `renderer.sceneDepth`, so the frame draws the depth prepass); "quarter": a quarter resolution without history, RGBA8 (radiance as c / (c + 1)) where half-float targets do not render; "dome": a 2D cloud dome from the weather map; "off": clear sky.

### RainTier

*type*

```ts
export type RainTier = "full" | "reduced" | "minimal" | "off";
```

"full": a 512² cover map over 128 m, three rings of four layers of drops, splashes and drips; "reduced": a 256² map, two layers, no drips; "minimal": no cover map (the game's shelter boxes alone), two rings of two layers; "off": no drops (surfaces still wet).

### VolumetricClouds

*class*

Volumetric clouds (Schneider 2015, Hillaire 2016): the sky layer `weather_clouds`, marched through Perlin-Worley (128³) and Worley (32³) noise the CPU bakes a few rows a frame (`noiseRows`; the "dome" tier until then) over a weather map whose coverage is ranked through its own CDF; a two-lobe phase, multiple-scattering octaves, diffusion through deep cloud, skylight and the ground's bounce; their shadow on the ground (WeatherEffects' light hook) and a panorama the sky's environment and aerial passes read (overcast dims the skylight). Its tier is lowered to the device and graphics level with a note in Options → Graphics.

```ts
export class VolumetricClouds { … }
```

- `private constructor();`
- `requestedTier: CloudTier;`
- `readonly tier: CloudTier;`

- `noiseRows: number;`

  Shape-noise rows baked a frame (default 32, at most 128; the "dome" tier until baked).

- `readonly ready: boolean;`

  Whether the noise volumes are baked.

- `readonly coverageCdf: Float32Array;`

  The weather map's coverage CDF, 256 entries.

- `readonly hookUniforms: { wxcShadowMap: { value: Texture | null }; wxcShadowArea: { value: Vector4 } };`

  The light hook's uniforms (`wxcShadowMap`, `wxcShadowArea`).

- `static deviceTier(): CloudTier;`
- `readonly shaderError: string | null;`
- `compile(): void;`
- `dispose(): void;`

### Rain

*class*

Rain (Solstice's): drops placed by a hash and the clock, nothing simulated, carried by the mean wind and falling at Gunn and Kinzer's speeds in Marshall and Palmer's numbers, each a streak over 1/45 s; splashes and drips from eaves; none under what stands over them (a cover map drawn from above, or `setShelters`).

  Set when what stands in the rain moved (it is redrawn anyway when the camera moves 16 m).

- `coverRoot: Object3D | null;`

  What casts the cover map (default the scene).

  Where drops splash where nothing was drawn (sea level; default -Infinity: none).

- `readonly coverTarget: WebGLRenderTarget | null;`

  The cover map (heights under its top, 16 bits in red and green) and the rain map made from it (height, hollow depth in blue, eave in alpha), for inspection; null without one.

- `readonly mapTarget: WebGLRenderTarget | null;`

- `setShelters(boxes: readonly Box3[]): this;`

### Lightning

*class*

Lightning (Rakov and Uman, after Solstice): strikes as a Poisson process at the weather's `thunder` rate, 0.6–9 km off, a third to the ground with one to five return strokes 30–90 ms apart and a branching bolt drawn as additive ribbons; the flash lights the sky and clouds and the scene (its DirectionalLight `light`, by the square of the distance); thunder (filtered noise rendered offline by the engine's audio) heard after the flash by the distance at 343 m/s.

```ts
export class Lightning { … }
```

- `private constructor();`
- `readonly state: Float64Array;`
- `readonly light: DirectionalLight;`
- `readonly bolt: Mesh;`

- `flashIntensity: number;`

  The flash light's intensity for a flash 2 km off at its peak (default 4; it shines from the cloud deck above the flash); its glow in the sky (default 2); thunder's loudness (default 1, 0 silent).

- `skyGlow: number;`
- `thunderVolume: number;`
- `onStrike: ((strike: Strike, thunderDelay: number) => void) | null;`

- `strikeSoon(): this;`

  A strike at the next update, 1.5–4 km ahead.

- `readonly strike: Strike | null;`
- `readonly strikes: number;`

- `readonly holdsExposure: boolean;`

  A flash, until just after its last stroke: exposure holds. The lightning sets `renderer.exposure.hold` for it (and clears it after; never a hold the game set itself), so automatic exposure (`renderer.exposure.auto`) neither darkens for the flash nor brightens after it.

- `readonly shaderError: string | null;`
- `compile(): void;`
- `dispose(): void;`

### WeatherEffectsOptions

*interface*

```ts
export interface WeatherEffectsOptions { … }
```

- `weather?: Weather | WeatherSettings | WeatherKind;`

  The starting weather (default "fair").

- `cycle?: boolean | { seed?: number };`

  The sky changes by itself from the starting kind (default false).

- `sky?: import("starhermit:sky").SkyAtmosphere | null;`

  The SkyAtmosphere the clouds join (none: no clouds).

- `wind?: WindField | null;`

  A WindField the weather drives: half the cloud-height wind, its gusts and turbulence.

- `clouds?: CloudTier;`

  Tiers asked for (default "full"), each lowered to the device.

- `rain?: RainTier;`

- `lightning?: boolean;`

  Lightning and thunder (default true each); the lightning's seed.

- `thunder?: boolean;`
- `seed?: number;`

- `autoExposure?: boolean;`

  Adapt the exposure to the weather (default false). Where automatic exposure runs (`renderer.capabilities.screenEffects` is set) this defers to it: it turns `renderer.exposure.auto` on (with a sky `{ night: { minEv: 1, maxEv: 15 }, daylight: sky }`, so night stays dark; a game's own settings are kept) and off again, and the lightning holds it through flashes. Elsewhere (the fallback) it eases `renderer.toneMappingExposure` with the clouds' dimming, held through flashes.

### WeatherEffects

*class*

The weather and its effects, an Object3D the game adds to the scene (it holds the rain, the bolt and the flash's light); `update` once a frame after moving the camera, before rendering. Lit materials take its `hooks` (or `apply(root)`): the clouds' shadow on the sun and wet surfaces (Lagarde: porous surfaces darken as their pores fill, then a film turns them glossy; puddles in the hollows of level ground, filled while it rains and drained after, faster in wind, ringed by drops; streaks down walls; nothing under a roof).

### RAIN\_RINGS\_WGSL

*const*

```ts
export const RAIN_RINGS_WGSL: string;
```

WGSL for water's own hooks: `rain_rings(xz, time, density, footprint) -> vec3f`, the slope rain's rings give the water (x, z) and the mean square slope it adds to its roughness (z), seen by a pixel `footprint` metres across; with `Rain.ringUniforms`' (seconds, density).
